A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learn2Synth and provide the main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material needed for comparison. Retained content can be matched across relocations and section renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic noise and intensity-nonuniformity experiments, real MRI segmentation evaluations, and supplementary validation-selection and unpaired-segmentation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds AdvChain comparisons, nnUNet backbone results, and a fixed-test-size comparison in Tables 5, 8, and 9.

M1.justification: The alternating synthetic/real passes, hypergradient updates, and parametric and nonparametric augmentation procedures remain unchanged. The supplementary GAN-based unpaired approach already appears in v2. nnUNet is an additional backbone evaluation of the existing training strategy.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic scenarios and ABIDE, OASIS3, Buckner39, and FreeSurfer maintenance data, including the same FLASH contrasts. The added experiments retain this coverage. Three-dimensional segmentation, registration, and lesion detection are discussed only as future possibilities.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds AdvChain as an evaluated comparator on ABIDE and OASIS3. Table 9 adds Mixed SynthSeg and Finetuned SynthSeg to the Buckner39/FLASH comparison; in v2 these comparators appeared only in the ABIDE/OASIS3 comparison. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 11 adds evaluations using nnUNet for both Learn2Synth and Naive SynthSeg. Table 9 fixes the supervised and Learn2Synth MPRAGE test counts at five across training sizes, whereas retained Table 6 uses five, 29, or 33 test examples. Relocated split descriptions are unchanged; newly specified baseline augmentations are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Table 8 adds a check of whether Learn2Synth's advantage persists with another segmentation backbone. Table 9 adds a control addressing differing test-set sizes. The synthetic noise/INU analyses, validation-selection comparison, and unpaired-segmentation experiment are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The uncertainty reporting in Tables 6 and 7 is unchanged, and Table 9 follows the existing plus/minus reporting practice. Neither version specifies additional seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence-interval procedures, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Previously reported entries in Tables 1–7 remain unchanged. Table 5 adds AdvChain Dice scores of 0.867/0.848 on ABIDE/OASIS3. Table 8 reports nnUNet-based Learn2Synth at 0.893/0.875 versus Naive SynthSeg at 0.881/0.863. Table 9 adds comparator and fixed-test-size results; its revised MPRAGE values represent different test conditions, not same-setting performance gains. Training-time measurements are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, the hypergradient derivation, and the augmentation distributions retain the same mathematical content. The new discussions of computational efficiency and three-dimensional applicability introduce no formal theorem, proof, or revised assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about learning synthesis parameters, avoiding direct real-data training of the segmenter, and improving segmentation and contrast generalization. The added experiments supply further support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: New supplementary discussion addresses the nnUNet accuracy/runtime tradeoff and argues that hypergradient optimization avoids costly augmentation searches. It also discusses anisotropy and memory demands for future 3D use and explicitly limits demonstrated applicability to segmentation. The requirement for labeled target-modality scans remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: Section 8 newly specifies intensity and spatial augmentations applied to baselines. Section 13 discloses 1,500 epochs, batch size 64, an L40S GPU, CPU/RAM specifications, and approximately 17.7 versus 10.3 training hours for Learn2Synth and Naive SynthSeg on OASIS3. Existing architecture, optimizer, preprocessing, and code-access information is largely relocated, not newly supplied.

R1.justification: The same 90 cited works and substantive related-work discussion are retained. AdvChain's source, reference 14, was already cited in v2; its new experimental participation is a baseline change. Changes to reference 66 update bibliographic presentation rather than the cited work or research positioning.

P1.justification: Implementation and dataset-protocol paragraphs move from Section 4 into supplementary Section 8, which also incorporates v2's architecture section. Supplementary sections are expanded and renumbered, with limited grammar, affiliation, and acknowledgment edits. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8 and 9, expands Table 5 with an AdvChain row, and relocates existing figures and tables as the document reflows. Figures 1–5 retain their scientific content; the principal visual changes concern placement and the additional tabular displays.

improvement.justification: The added comparator, backbone check, and fixed-test-size analysis strengthen evaluation of the existing claims, while the new training and hardware details improve reproducibility and make computational costs assessable. These gains are limited: the core findings remain unchanged, main-text Table 6 still uses varying test sizes, and Table 9 reports the controlled cross-contrast comparison only for FLASH 3 degrees.
